name: mirage
text: Estimate: moderate, about a weekend or 3-6 hours with software, and annoying mainly because of two things. Not hard: Ally savings/spending (a 1099-INT at most), debit cards and Cash App personal (not taxable unless it is income; Cash App only sends a 1099-K for business-type payments), gifts from family (not income to you; the giver may owe a gift tax form only if over about $19k per person a year, not you), no kids. Real work: (1) Ally Invest with lots of daily trading. The 1099-B can have thousands of lines, but the broker reports it to the IRS and tax software imports it. Check for wash sales (selling at a loss and re-buying within 30 days; losses get disallowed), which is the usual source of surprise tax bills. (2) Gambling: BetMGM sends a W-2G or 1099 only for big single wins, but you report all winnings anyway. Novig and Kalshi may or may not send forms, so you download the account history yourself. This is the sticky part: the IRS taxes gross winnings, and losses only offset them if you itemize. So you could be down overall and still owe tax on winnings with no deduction for losses. That is why the standard deduction decision matters. Do ask a preparer about it. (3) Two states: Maryland resident return, plus a New Jersey nonresident return for NJ-source income, with a Maryland credit for NJ tax. If you actually LIVE in NJ and only keep a Maryland home, your residency could be NJ instead, which flips the setup. A one-time CPA visit (about $200-500) is worth it to settle that. Also: with no earned income, check whether family is claiming you as a dependent. Nothing here is hard, only tedious, and the records are what make it easy: save the yearly Novig, BetMGM and Kalshi exports and the Ally 1099-B. General info only, not tax advice.
